subject: radiology
title: Thrombolysis and thrombectomy

steps.tx: Fresh thrombus dissolves with lytic treatment, while old organised clot resists drugs and needs a different plan. A viable limb with symptoms under **14 days** suits **catheter directed thrombolysis** through a multi sidehole catheter in the clot. The infusion uses **alteplase** with heparin cover, and serial angiographic checks track progress during treatment. A limb with audible Doppler signals and no fixed mottling stays viable and suits catheter treatment well. An **embolic occlusion** with a clear source lyses faster than thrombosis that forms on diseased plaque.
steps.say: Fresh thrombus dissolves with lytic treatment while old organised clot resists drugs and needs another plan. A viable limb with recent symptoms suits catheter lysis through a multi sidehole catheter inside clot. The infusion uses a lytic drug with heparin cover and serial checks track progress during treatment. A limb with audible signals and no fixed mottling stays viable and suits catheter treatment. An embolic blockage with a clear source lyses faster than thrombosis on diseased plaque.

steps.tx: This knee angiogram shows a **multi sidehole lysis catheter** that crosses an occluded popliteal segment during catheter directed treatment. Contrast stops with a **meniscus sign** at the upper edge of thrombus, which marks fresh clot rather than chronic disease. Faint **runoff vessels** reappear below the knee and those vessels show that lytic treatment has begun to restore flow. The image matters for the exam because catheter position inside clot decides drug contact and success. Serial checks then judge whether flow improves enough to stop the infusion safely.
steps.say: This knee angiogram shows a multi sidehole catheter that crosses an occluded popliteal segment during treatment. steps.tx: Technique and monitoring decide safety during thrombolysis, because the same drug that clears clot also causes bleeding. **Ultrasound accelerated catheters** and pulse spray speed lysis, although proven superiority over standard infusion remains absent. The team follows **fibrinogen monitoring** with dose reduction or pause when levels fall sharply during infusion. **Puncture site bleeding** occurs most often and the team manages that bleeding with pressure and dose review. **Intracranial bleeding** remains rare but catastrophic, so any suggestion ends the infusion at once without delay.

steps.tx: Pulmonary embolism treatment escalates by risk, and blood pressure sorts the urgency before any drug starts. A **high risk embolism** with hypotension receives **systemic thrombolysis** when no contraindication blocks that rescue treatment. **Catheter directed therapy** with fragmentation, aspiration or local lysis suits a massive embolism when systemic lysis stays banned. Stable disease with right heart strain usually stays anticoagulated, with escalation only when deterioration appears. **Phlegmasia cerulea dolens** with venous gangrene threatens the limb and justifies catheter removal of the clot burden.
steps.say: Pulmonary embolism treatment escalates by risk and blood pressure sorts the urgency before any drug starts. A high risk embolism with low pressure receives systemic lysis when no contraindication blocks rescue. Catheter therapy with fragmentation or aspiration suits a massive embolism when systemic lysis stays banned. Stable disease with heart strain usually stays anticoagulated with escalation only when deterioration appears. Venous gangrene threatens the limb and justifies catheter removal of the clot burden urgently.

steps.tx: Some patients must never receive lytic treatment, because bleeding risk outweighs any possible clot benefit completely. **Absolute contraindications** include prior intracranial bleeding, recent ischaemic stroke, active bleeding and recent brain or spine surgery. Recent major surgery, trauma, gut bleeding and severe hypertension demand careful case by case judgement. **Pregnancy and the postpartum period** raise bleeding risk sharply and need senior multidisciplinary input before treatment. Routine deep vein lysis stays selective after trial evidence showed limited benefit against bleeding, favouring young low risk limbs.
